name: runtime-rss-units
goal: Record process peak RSS in bytes across Bun and Node without accepting the macOS Bun scaling error.

evidence: Raw Bun 1.2.18 on Darwin reports rss 23,199,744 bytes and maxRSS 23,232,512, while Node 25.9 reports rss 47,497,216 bytes and maxRSS 46,384 KiB. The shared profiler multiplies both by 1024, producing impossible 300GB Bun observations.

Existing profile and runner tests require positive memory only. Extend the normal Vitest/Bun runner fixture to record independent fresh-process RSS byte references and bound recorded peaks to that scale; extend the existing real rank boundary case to reject impossible multi-gigabyte memory for its tiny fresh workload.

bf56ed73f proof 9ded5d0c records two real failures: the source runner reports 113,833,410,560 bytes against a fresh-process scale bound of 889,454,592; the real rank process reports 335,728,869,376 bytes against its 8GiB sanity ceiling. Other cases pass. These are unit-scale guards, not wider performance budgets.

Centralize true process-peak RSS conversion in the existing profiling service. Preserve Bun/Darwin native bytes; convert the KiB reports from Node and other supported hosts. Reuse it for sampled observations, repeated profiles, unit benchmarks and history-index workloads. Mark the corrected memory method explicitly and retain old records unchanged.
